text: Yesterday I walked to the village with my friend.
tip: 'walked' ends in /t/: /wɔːkt/. It is one syllable, not 'walk-ed'. The 'l' is silent too!

text: We visited my grandparents last weekend.
tip: After t or d, -ed adds a syllable: VIS-it-ed /ˈvɪzɪtɪd/.

text: She played the piano at the party.
tip: 'played' is one syllable /pleɪd/. Stress pi-A-no and PAR-ty.

text: I'm going to buy some sweets tomorrow.
tip: Keep 'to' short and weak: /ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə/. Stress SWEETS and to-MOR-row.

text: The castle is bigger than our school.
tip: 'than' is weak /ðən/. Stress the important words: CAS-tle, BIG-ger, SCHOOL.

text: Could you tell me the way to the station?
tip: 'Could you' joins into /kʊdʒu/. Stress WAY and STA-tion.

text: It was the best day of my life.
tip: Stress BEST, DAY and LIFE. Say 'of my' quickly and lightly.

text: There's a bakery next to the post office.
tip: In 'next to', say just one /t/: /neks tə/. Stress BAK-er-y and POST of-fice.

text: He usually has cereal for breakfast.
tip: 'usually' /ˈjuːʒuəli/ has the soft /ʒ/ sound from 'television'. 'breakfast' is BREK-fust.

text: My sister is taller than me.
tip: Stress TALL-er. British English doesn't say the final r: /ˈtɔːlə/.

text: We're going to the beach if it's sunny.
tip: 'We're' /wɪə/ and 'it's' /ɪts/ are one beat each. Don't confuse 'beach' /iː/ with a short /ɪ/.

text: I've never eaten candy floss before.
tip: 'I've' is a quick /aɪv/. Link 'never eaten' with an r: 'neve-reaten'.

text: What did you do at the weekend?
tip: 'did you' often sounds like /dɪdʒu/. British English says 'at the weekend'.

text: The shop opens at nine and closes at six.
tip: 'opens' ends in /z/. 'closes' has an extra syllable: /ˈkləʊzɪz/.

text: I want to learn how to make chocolate.
tip: Both 'to's are weak /tə/. 'chocolate' has two syllables: /ˈtʃɒklət/.

text: My little brother was frightened of the dragon.
tip: 'frightened' has two syllables /ˈfraɪtnd/. Stress DRAG-on.

text: Can I have a glass of water, please?
tip: In British English 'glass' has a long /ɑː/ and 'water' is /ˈwɔːtə/ with a clear /t/.

text: The weather was cold, so we stayed inside.
tip: 'weather' is /ˈweðə/: round lips, then tongue between teeth. 'stayed' is one syllable.

text: Which one is cheaper, the red one or the blue one?
tip: Your voice goes up on 'red one' and down on 'blue one'. That's how English offers a choice.

text: I usually walk to school, but today I took the bus.
tip: Stress the contrast: WALK … but … BUS.

text: She's wearing a beautiful purple dress.
tip: BEAU-ti-ful /ˈbjuːtɪfl/ has three syllables with stress on the first. PUR-ple.

text: Thirteen thirsty frogs jumped into the pond.
tip: Lots of /θ/! thir-TEEN is stressed at the end. 'jumped' ends in /t/: /dʒʌmpt/.

text: We're going to the beach on Saturday.
tip: 'going to' often sounds like /ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə/. Stress BEACH and SAT-ur-day.

text: My best friend lives next door.
tip: Join 'best friend': the /t/ almost disappears, /bes frend/. Stress NEXT DOOR.

text: Could you pass me the salt, please?
tip: 'Could you' links into /kʊdʒu/. Let your voice go up a little on 'please'.

text: Yesterday it snowed for the first time.
tip: 'snowed' ends with a soft /d/: /snəʊd/. Don't add an extra syllable!

text: I usually have cereal for breakfast.
tip: Stress U-su-al-ly and BREAK-fast. 'cereal' sounds like /ˈsɪəriəl/.

text: The museum opens at half past nine.
tip: Stress mu-SE-um. 'half past' has a long /ɑː/ twice: /hɑːf pɑːst/.

text: My brother is taller than me.
tip: 'than' is weak /ðən/. Stress TALL-er and ME.

text: We watched a funny film last night.
tip: 'watched' is one syllable ending in /tʃt/: /wɒtʃt/.

text: How much does this T-shirt cost?
tip: Wh- questions go down at the end. Stress MUCH and COST.

text: I've got a headache and a sore throat.
tip: 'throat' starts with /θr/: tongue between your teeth, then /r/. 'ache' sounds like /eɪk/.

text: Turn left at the end of the street.
tip: Link 'end of the': /end əv ðə/. Stress LEFT and STREET.

text: There are lots of shells on the beach.
tip: 'shells' /ʃelz/ and 'beach' /biːtʃ/: keep the vowel in 'beach' long.

text: She's practising the piano for her concert.
tip: Stress PRAC-tis-ing, pi-AN-o and CON-cert.

text: Don't forget your umbrella today.
tip: 'Don't' is one beat /dəʊnt/. Stress um-BREL-la.

text: Our cat climbed up the apple tree.
tip: The 'b' in 'climbed' is silent: /klaɪmd/.

text: Would you like to come to my party?
tip: 'Would you' links into /wʊdʒu/. Your voice goes up on PAR-ty?

text: The train was late, so we waited.
tip: 'waited' adds a syllable: WAIT-id /ˈweɪtɪd/, because 'wait' ends in /t/.

text: I'm saving my pocket money for a skateboard.
tip: Stress POCK-et MON-ey and SKATE-board. 'saving' has /eɪ/.

text: I went to the farm and fed the goats.
tip: 'went' and 'fed' are short and quick. 'goats' has /əʊ/ and ends /ts/.

text: We baked cookies for the school fair.
tip: 'baked' is one syllable ending in /kt/: /beɪkt/. Not 'bake-ed'!

text: My little sister is afraid of spiders.
tip: Stress a-FRAID and SPI-ders. 'of' is weak: /əv/.

text: Are you coming to the swimming pool later?
tip: Let your voice go UP at the end: LA-ter? 'Are you' is quick: /ə ju/.

text: It's colder today than it was yesterday.
tip: Stress COLD-er. 'than' and 'was' are weak: /ðən/, /wəz/.

text: I need to finish my homework before dinner.
tip: 'to' is weak /tə/. Stress FIN-ish, HOME-work and DIN-ner.

text: Mum bought me a new pair of trainers.
tip: 'bought' sounds like 'sort' /bɔːt/: the 'gh' is silent. 'pair' sounds like 'pear'.

text: The library is closed on Sundays.
tip: 'closed' is one syllable: /kləʊzd/. Stress LI-bra-ry and SUN-days.

text: We had a picnic under the big oak tree.
tip: Link 'had a' into /hædə/ and 'big oak' into /bɪɡəʊk/.

text: What time does the film start?
tip: Wh- questions go down at the end. 'does the' is quick and weak.

text: My favourite subject at school is science.
tip: The 'c' after 's' in 'science' is silent: /ˈsaɪəns/. Stress FA-vour-ite.

text: I'm sorry I'm late for the lesson.
tip: Say 'sorry' warmly with a fall: SOR-ry. 'I'm' is one beat: /aɪm/.

text: He fell off his bike and hurt his knee.
tip: The 'k' in 'knee' is silent: /niː/. 'hurt' has /ɜː/.

text: There isn't any juice left in the fridge.
tip: 'juice' starts with /dʒ/ and 'fridge' ends with it. 'isn't' is /ˈɪznt/.

text: First, mix the flour and the eggs.
tip: Pause after 'First,'. 'flour' sounds just like 'flower' /ˈflaʊə/.

text: Let's make a snowman in the garden!
tip: 'Let's' is one beat /lets/. Stress SNOW-man and GAR-den.

text: Have you ever been to the seaside?
tip: 'been' is weak and quick /bɪn/. Your voice goes UP on SEA-side?

text: My grandpa grows tomatoes and carrots.
tip: 'grows' and 'tomatoes' both have /əʊ/. Stress to-MA-toes.

text: The baby penguins were sliding on the ice.
tip: 'were' is weak /wə/. Stress PEN-guins and SLI-ding.

text: We clapped and cheered at the end of the show.
tip: 'clapped' ends in /t/, 'cheered' ends in /d/. Both are one syllable!
